scope: Standalone opt-in WASM slow-exit contract for protected 32-bit 80386 AT; no dispatcher or default-path integration

contract.decodedBytes: Only flat protected-32 two-byte MOV r32,[base] and MOV [base],r32 with ModR/M mod 00 and no SIB/displacement; code page and bytes are checked at entry
contract.mirror: Only explicit already-valid CPU _translations are copied into a 64-slot direct-mapped WASM TLB, keyed by linear page, translation generation, CR3 and CR4; user, writable, dirty and separate store-admission bits are checked per access
contract.fastAccess: One 32-bit access wholly inside a cached ordinary kind-1 RAM page above 1 MiB; direct store also requires cached dirty/writable translation and excludes tracked page tables and all code pages registered with this spike
contract.slowExit: WASM returns the number of already completed instructions and exits before any missing, unclean, cross-page, permission-failing, MMIO/ROM, tracked-code or page-table write access; ordinary JS executes the next instruction and owns page walk, A/D change, fault and MMIO behavior
contract.eventBoundary: The wrapper clips the WASM budget to existing AT chip and LAPIC deadlines and refuses pending IRQ/NMI/debug and other interpreter-only states
contract.mirrorValidationCost: O(number of mirrored entries) before each native call, bounded by 64; the 128-call workload with two mirrored entries performed 256 validity checks. This cost has not been measured against full xv6 and could erase any gain. No full 512-entry JS TLB copy occurs per call.
contract.integrationRequirement: A future dispatcher must register every cached code page and arrange incremental mirroring of relevant existing JS translations. This standalone spike is not an automatic or general 386 memory accelerator.

differentialValidation.cases: Dependent cached read; second-page miss and JS walk; second-page #PF and CR2; CPL0-mirrored supervisor page refused at CPL3 for both read (#PF code 5) and write (#PF code 7); clean D-bit write fallback; dirty RAM store parity; registered code and page-table store refusal; cross-page read exit; CR3/generation staleness; MMIO refusal; current-code-page store refusal; chip deadline; store feeding later same-page and dependent next-page loads

boundedWorkload.program: MOV EAX,[EBX]; MOV ECX,[EAX] over two cached data pages
boundedWorkload.result: Register, flags, EIP, CPU/board cycles, chip debt and complete 4 MiB RAM SHA-256 equal to ordinary machine.step() after each bounded run

limits: No full xv6, FreeDOS, or Windows workload was run with this spike because it has no dispatcher integration. The bounded differential proof is not RTx, a CPU-time benchmark, or evidence of a 10x gain. Individual accesses are same-page only; dependent addresses may use different already-mirrored pages. A future integrated implementation needs full guest/RAM parity and paired user-CPU A/B before any speed claim.
